statement: SK hynix and Sandisk released the first High Bandwidth Flash technical specification through the Open Compute Project, covering capacities up to 512GB in 8-high and 16-high NAND stacks, three performance grades from about 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s, and a UCIe chiplet interface, with Google and Tenstorrent joining the consortium.
why: A standardised flash-based memory tier at hundreds of gigabytes and terabyte-per-second bandwidth is a candidate relief valve for the HBM shortage, though a published specification is years away from shipping capacity.

impact.mechanism: An open standard for high-bandwidth flash creates a possible alternative memory tier alongside HBM, which over time could ease the memory constraint on AI accelerators.

evidence.excerpt: capacity 'up to 512GB based on two stack configurations (8-high and 16-high NAND dies)'; three performance grades delivering 'approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s'

confidence.basis: Company press release distributed through a newswire and captured at secondary tier; a specification announcement is not evidence of shipping supply.

dispersion: Figures are specification ceilings and performance grade ranges, not shipped product volumes, so no value is recorded.
